description: Angesichts struktureller, demografischer und klimatischer Veränderungen steht die Innenstadt Bad Pyrmonts vor einem umfassenden Transformationsprozess. Veränderungen im Einzelhandel, zunehmende Leerstände, Defizite im öffentlichen Raum sowie höhere Anforderungen an Klimaanpassung und nachhaltige Mobilität erfordern eine integrierte Weiterentwicklung. Seit 2022 ist die Innenstadt daher in das Städtebauförderprogramm "Lebendige Zentren" eingebunden. Grundlage des Wettbewerbs ist das Integrierte Städtebauliche Entwicklungskonzept (ISEK) mit dem Leitbild "Gesundheitsstandort mit viel Geschichte". Ziel ist eine zukunftsfähige, lebendige und multifunktionale Innenstadt. Dazu gehören insbesondere die Stärkung als Wohn-, Versorgungs- und Gesundheitsstandort, die Weiterentwicklung des Tourismus, die Revitalisierung von Leerständen sowie die Ergänzung von Freizeit-, Kultur- und Naherholungsangeboten. Mit dem Wettbewerb sollen innovative und umsetzungsorientierte Konzepte für die frei- und stadträumliche Entwicklung gewonnen werden. Im Mittelpunkt stehen klimaangepasste Freiraumstrukturen, eine höhere Aufenthalts- und Nutzungsqualität, nachhaltige Mobilität, die Aktivierung der Innenstadt durch neue Nutzungen, temporäre Interventionen und flexible Nutzungskonzepte sowie die Berücksichtigung aller Generationen und Nutzergruppen. Aufbauend auf bereits umgesetzten Maßnahmen soll ein langfristig tragfähiges Entwicklungskonzept entstehen, das kurzfristige Impulse setzt und die schrittweise Umsetzung der ISEK-Maßnahmen innerhalb der kommenden zehn Jahre ermöglicht.

Der Höchstwert der Rahmenvereinbarung beträgt 2.200.000,00 EUR netto. Die im Leistungsverzeichnis (Anlage B.1.1) angegebenen Mengen sind unverbindliche Schätzmengen und begründen weder eine Mindestabnahmeverpflichtung noch einen An-spruch auf den Abruf bestimmter Mengen. Dieser Höchstwert gilt für die gesamte Vertragslaufzeit einschließlich sämtlicher Verlänge-rungsoptionen und damit für eine maximale Gesamtlaufzeit von acht Jahren. Mit Erreichen des Höchstwerts endet die Möglichkeit weiterer Abrufe aus der Rahmenvereinbarung, auch wenn die maximale Vertragslaufzeit zu diesem Zeitpunkt noch nicht abgelaufen ist.

title: Netherlands – Engineering works and construction works – Realisatie Civieltechnisch bouwwerk t.b.v. procesinstallatie (CO2 capture plant) bij HVC Alkmaar
description: HVC heeft zichzelf als doel gesteld dat er in 2035 één miljoen ton CO2 minder wordt uitgestoten dan in 2025. Dit willen o.a. realiseren door op HVC-locatie Alkmaar een CO2 afvanginstallatie te ontwikkelen. Het doel van deze installatie is om 100 kiloton CO2 af te vangen en de opgevangen CO2 te verkopen (CCU). Ter vergelijking: dit komt overeen met de gemiddelde CO2 uitstoot van het energieverbruik van 30.816 huishoudens. In 2024 heeft HVC na een aanbestedingsprocedure een contract afgesloten met leverancier SLB Capturi | SLB Capturi (SLBC) voor de bouw van een CO2 afvanginstallatie op HVC-locatie in Alkmaar. De afgelopen periode heeft HVC samen met SLBC gewerkt aan een FEED (front-end engineering design). In juni 2026 is de FEED gereed. Leverancier SLBC van de afvanginstallatie heeft de civiele werkzaamheden en de Balance of plant, uitgesloten van zijn levering. Deze moeten door HVC zelf verzorgd worden. Hiervoor heeft HVC het initiatief genomen voor een drietal inkoopprojecten: • Engineering Bouwrijp maken en Civiel (Engineering) • Bouwrijp maken (BMR) • Civieltechnisch bouwwerk (Civiel) De Mercell omgeving, de leidraad en aanbestedingsprocedure heeft specifiek betrekking op het onderdeel: civieltechnische bouwwerk De Opdracht betreft, in het kort: De werkzaamheden omvatten de volledige civiel-bouwkundige realisatie van de nieuwbouw van de CO₂-afvanginstallatie op het terrein van HVC te Alkmaar. De opdracht bestaat uit het inrichten van de bouwplaats, het uitvoeren van tijdelijke voorzieningen en bemaling, het verrichten van sloop- en grondwerkzaamheden en het realiseren van terreininrichting en terreinverhardingen. Daarnaast omvat de opdracht de aanleg van hemelwater- en terreinriolering, drainagevoorzieningen, groenvoorzieningen en verkeersvoorzieningen. Verder omvat de opdracht het realiseren van funderingen voor de diverse procesinstallaties en gebouwen, waaronder funderingspalen, zware in het werk gestorte betonconstructies, fundatieplaten, kelderconstructies, vloeren, opstortingen en vloeistofkerende verhardingen. Tevens behoren de bouwkundige werkzaamheden voor het E-gebouw en het compressorgebouw tot de opdracht, inclusief metselwerk, prefab betonelementen, staalconstructies, gevels, daken, kozijnen, deuren en overige bouwkundige afwerkingen. Daarnaast is de aannemer verantwoordelijk voor de coördinatie van sparingen, doorvoeringen, instortvoorzieningen en de afstemming met de gebouwgebonden en installaties.

description: Försvarsmakten är en organisation som är i ständig förändring och detta medför ett behov att över tiden kunna genomföra modellering av hur den framtida organisationen och dess verksamhet ska se ut. description: 1. Przedmiotem zamówienia jest odbieranie, transport i zagospodarowanie całej masy odpadów komunalnych zmieszanych i selektywnie zebranych wskazanych w opisie zamówienia z wszystkich nieruchomości położonych na terenie Gminy Szczuczyn, na których zamieszkują mieszkańcy w sposób zapewniający osiągnięcie odpowiednich poziomów recyklingu, przygotowania do ponownego użycia i odzysku innymi metodami oraz ograniczenie masy odpadów komunalnych ulegających biodegradacji przekazywanych do składowania, zgodnie z zapisami ustawy z dnia 13 września 1996r. o utrzymaniu czystości i porządku w gminach, zapisami aktualnego Planu Gospodarki Odpadami Województwa Podlaskiego oraz przepisami Regulaminu utrzymania czystości i porządku na terenie Gminy Szczuczyn. Liczba gospodarstw z których odbierane będą odpady może ulec zmianie w trakcie trwania umowy. Zamawiający na bieżąco będzie przekazywał informacje niezbędne do prawidłowego wykonania umowy. Obowiązkiem wykonawcy będzie realizacja zamówienia z uwzględnieniem zmian w ramach zaoferowanej kwoty za wykonania usługi. 2. Wykonawca podczas realizacji zamówienia zobowiązany jest: 1) zagospodarować odebrane od właścicieli nieruchomości odpady komunalne zgodnie z obowiązującymi przepisami w szczególności ustawą o odpadach, ustawą o utrzymaniu czystości i porządku w gminach, regulaminem utrzymania czystości i porządku na terenie Gminy Szczuczyn oraz wojewódzkim planem gospodarki odpadami, obowiązującym w czasie trwania umowy. 2) wskazać w ofercie instalacje, do której będzie przekazywać odebrane odpady komunalne. Charakterystyka Gminy Szczuczyn w kontekście wyceny przedmiotu zamówienia: 1) powierzchnia Gminy Szczuczyn wynosi 11560 ha, 2) Gmina składa się z miasta Szczuczyn i 29 sołectw (szacuje się, że do 3 % stanowi zabudowa kolonijna i w przysiółkach). Wykonawca ma obowiązek przed złożeniem oferty zapoznać się ze specyfiką gminy tj. z rozmieszczeniem nieruchomości zamieszkałych, ukształtowaniem terenu oraz systemem dróg gminy Szczuczyn w celu poprawnej wyceny zamówienia, 3) liczba zameldowanych mieszkańców Gminy Szczuczyn wynosi 5649 osoby (w tym na wsi: 2641, w mieście: 3008)- dane na dzień 31.07.2026r., 4) systemem zbiórki odpadów komunalnych objęto wszystkie nieruchomości zamieszkałe na terenie Gminy Szczuczyn, 5) łączna liczba złożonych deklaracji na dzień przygotowania opisu przedmiotu zamówienia wynosi 1167 i obejmuje 4 221 osób. W związku z tym Wykonawca zobowiązany będzie do uwzględnienia zmian w harmonogramie odbiorów. Zmiany te nie mogą mieć wpływu na wysokość złożonej przez Przedsiębiorcę oferty w odniesieniu do zaproponowanych stawek odbioru odpadów z poszczególnych typów gospodarstw domowych w całym czasie realizacji przedmiotowego zamówienia. 5. title: Sources Sought: The Dalles Dam Gate Repair Pit Fire Protection and Life Safety Upgrades
description: General. This is a Sources Sought and is for informational/market research purposes only. This is not a Request for Proposals, Quotations, or an Invitation for Bids. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to obtain information regarding the interest, capabilities, capacity, and qualifications of industry so the Government can make informed business decisions. We are seeking responses from both large and small businesses, including Small Businesses, Small Disadvantaged Businesses, 8(a) participants, Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) firms, Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) concerns, Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) firms, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) concerns and Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) entities. All interested parties are encouraged to respond. Project Background. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Portland District (NWP) is seeking interested and capable sources with the technical expertise, personnel, and equipment necessary to perform electrical, life-safety, and fire-protection system modifications within the Powerhouse Gate Repair Pit at The Dalles Lock and Dam. The Gate Repair Pit is currently classified as a space that is not normally occupied. This requirement will modify the area to support its classification as a normally occupied space by correcting identified deficiencies in the existing fire-protection and life-safety systems and bringing the facility into compliance with applicable fire and safety codes. Project Scope. The work consists of three primary areas: electrical, life-safety, and fire-protection improvements. Incidental and supporting work is anticipated to include concrete penetrations; conduit, cable, and piping removal and installation; demolition and replacement or modification of wall-mounted electrical panels and doors; and integration of new fire-protection components with the Powerhouse�s existing fire-detection system. Electrical work includes general electrical repairs and modifications, including relocation of terminal boxes; rewiring of the welder control panel; modification of electrical enclosures and wall plates; relocation and modification of existing welding receptacles, including associated cable installation and minor cover-plate fabrication; and evaluation, replacement, rewiring, and reconfiguration of the blower electrical switch. The life-safety work includes furnishing and installing fire extinguishers, eyewash stations, gas-cylinder storage-limit markings, floor-level identification markings, and retractable doorway caution barriers, necessary to achieve compliance with applicable OSHA and NFPA requirements. The work also includes furnishing and installing protective plates for the existing oxygen and acetylene cylinders. The fire-protection work includes removal of the existing Gate Repair Pit entry door and installation of NFPA-rated fire doors; installation of siren/strobe notification appliances; repair, replacement, or reinforcement of firestopping at wall penetrations; and installation of fiber-optic heat-detection systems along the interior walls of the pit. The work also includes programming and integrating the fire-detection system to initiate damper closure and blower-motor shutdown upon fire detection, including all required cable, conduit, relays, controls, and associated devices. Project Location. The construction work will be performed at the Dalles Lock and Dam near The Dalles, Oregon, in Klickitat County Washington. Contractor access to the work site is on the Oregon side of the Columbia River from exit 88 on I-84. Project Purpose. The purpose of this project is to correct identified life-safety and fire-protection deficiencies within the Powerhouse Gate Repair Pit at The Dalles Lock and Dam, allowing the space to be safely classified and operated as normally occupied and bringing the facility into compliance with applicable OSHA, NFPA, fire, and life-safety requirements. Project Objectives. Construct the required electrical, life-safety, and fire-protection improvements in accordance with the contract documents and applicable codes. Test, integrate, and commission the completed systems to verify safe and reliable operation. Complete the work safely and within the established project schedule while minimizing impacts to Powerhouse operations. NAICS. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code for this requirement is 237990; Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction with a small business size standard of $45M. Anticipated Construction Schedule. NWP anticipates issuing an Invitation for Bids (IFB) in approximately March of 2027, with contract award anticipated in July 2027. Construction is expected to commence in September 2027 and be completed by January 2028. CMMC. Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC). The solicitation is anticipated to require the contractor and/or subcontractor(s) information system to process, store, or transmit Federal Contract Information (FCI) and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), and will require the contractor and/or subcontractor(s) to comply with CMMC requirements. The CMMC level anticipated for the solicitation is: CMMC Level 2 (Self). Magnitude of Construction. The magnitude of construction is anticipated to be between $1M and $5M. Project Specific Constraints and Challenges. Construction activities should be planned with the expectation that the Gate Repair Pit may remain occupied during performance of this contract. The Government intends to post occupancy notifications in a prominent location within or near the work area to inform personnel of ongoing occupancy. Submission Instructions. Submit your response to this notice via email to Aragon Liebzeit at Aragon.N.Liebzeit@usace.army.mil before 3:00 pm PT on 15 October 2026. Submission Content. Responses to this Sources Sought are limited to 8 pages and should include the following information: Firm name, physical address, point of contact, telephone number, email address, CAGE code, and Unique Entity ID (UEI). Applicable socioeconomic business classification(s). A description of the prime contractor�s relevant capabilities; specialized qualifications, licenses, certifications, and equipment; and the portion(s) of the anticipated work the firm intends to self-perform. The firm�s current CMMC level and anticipated date for achieving CMMC Level 2 Self-Assessment certification, if applicable. Joint-venture information, if applicable, including existing joint ventures and any potential joint-venture arrangements contemplated for this requirement. Bonding capacity, supported by a letter from the firm�s surety. A statement of the firm�s interest in the requirement and likelihood of submitting a bid in response to the future solicitation. Between 1 and 3 examples of completed projects that are similar in size, scope, and complexity to the requirement described in this Sources Sought notice. For joint ventures, identify projects completed by the joint-venture entity, if applicable. Please provide any additional information, recommendations, or concerns that you believe the Government should consider in developing its acquisition strategy for this requirement. For each submitted relevant project example, please include the following information: Project Title Contract Number Contract Award Date Customer name, phone number and email address Indicate if your firm was the prime contractor or a subcontractor. Please provide the prime contract number if your firm was a subcontractor. The construction work your firm completed for the project. Award value Final contract value Initial contract completion date Final contract completion date Please indicate the client�s satisfaction with the completed project Disclaimer and Important Notes. Service Description: The Government is seeking sources who can rebuild various material handling equipment (MHE) motors. The vendor would be required to pick up the motors at the Government location, provide all labor and materials to complete the motor rebuilds at their location, and once completed return the motors to the Government location. title: 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day
description: ? Celebrating Our 6th Annual Industry Day � Connecting Native-Owned Businesses with Albuquerque Area Indian Health Service (IHS) ? Monday, September 28 & Tuesday, September 29, 2026 ? 9:00 a.m. � 3:00 p.m. Mountain Daylight Time (MDT) ? Virtual Event | Microsoft Teams ?? FREE to Participate ? Space is limited. Registration will close once all vendor presentation slots have been filled. The Albuquerque Area Indian Health Service (IHS), Division of Contracts and Grants Management (DCGM), invites Native American-owned small businesses to participate in the 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day, a two-day virtual event dedicated to strengthening partnerships, expanding the Albuquerque Area IHS supplier base, and increasing awareness of the capabilities of Native American-owned businesses. Held shortly before Indigenous Peoples� Day, this event provides Native American-owned small businesses, including eligible Small Business Indian Firms (SBIFs) and Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs), an opportunity to introduce their organizations and showcase their capabilities directly to Albuquerque Area IHS acquisition professionals, program stakeholders, and organizational leadership. ?? Event Overview Day One will begin with introductions from Albuquerque Area IHS acquisition professionals and a brief overview of the Buy Indian Act and its role in supporting Indian economic enterprises through federal procurement. Following the opening session, participating vendors will receive an individually scheduled 10-minute presentation slot to introduce their businesses and highlight their capabilities, qualifications, products, services, past performance, and other information relevant to potential Albuquerque Area IHS requirements. Vendor capability presentations will continue throughout both days. ? Vendor Capability Presentations This is your opportunity to show Albuquerque Area IHS what your business can do! Each participating vendor will receive 10 minutes to present its capabilities directly to Albuquerque Area IHS personnel and other invited IHS acquisition and program professionals. Vendors are encouraged to use their presentation time to highlight information such as: Core capabilities and areas of expertise Products and/or services offered Relevant experience and past performance Geographic areas served Unique capabilities or solutions How your business can support IHS healthcare operations and mission requirements ? Who Will Be in the Audience? The Industry Day is designed to connect Native American-owned businesses with Albuquerque Area IHS personnel and other invited IHS acquisition and program professionals involved in identifying requirements, conducting market research, planning acquisitions, making purchases, and administering contracts. The audience may include: Buyers Contract Specialists Contracting Officers Contracting Officer�s Representatives (CORs) Government Purchase Cardholders and Approving Officials Service Unit Chief Executive Officers Program and technical personnel Albuquerque Area leadership This broad audience provides participating businesses an opportunity to increase awareness of their capabilities across IHS while helping acquisition and program personnel identify potential sources for future requirements. ? Why Participate? The Albuquerque Area IHS is committed to meaningful industry engagement and expanding opportunities for Native American-owned small businesses. Participation in Industry Day provides businesses an opportunity to: Introduce their company directly to IHS acquisition, program, and organizational personnel Increase awareness of their products, services, and capabilities Help IHS identify new and emerging industry capabilities Support IHS market research and acquisition planning Develop relationships with acquisition and program personnel Increase awareness of potential opportunities to do business with IHS At the same time, these interactions help Albuquerque Area IHS broaden its procurement base, identify qualified sources, increase competition, and strengthen relationships with the Native American-owned business community. We want to learn what your business can do for IHS. ? How to Participate Native American-owned small businesses interested in participating should email: ALBAreaSmallBusiness@ihs.gov Please indicate your interest in participating in the 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day and include your business name and primary point of contact. Upon receipt of your email, the Albuquerque Area IHS will provide a registration form to collect additional business information and assist with scheduling. Presentation times will be scheduled in advance. Each participating vendor will receive 10 minutes to present its capabilities, qualifications, products, and/or services. Space is limited, and registration will close once all available vendor presentation slots have been filled. Vendors are encouraged to register early. Additional event and Microsoft Teams information will be provided to registered participants prior to the event. ? Building Partnerships in Support of the IHS Mission Through the 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day, DCGM seeks to strengthen relationships with Native American-owned businesses, expand awareness of industry capabilities, broaden the Albuquerque Area procurement base, and identify qualified sources capable of supporting healthcare delivery. These partnerships help ensure that Albuquerque Area IHS acquisition professionals have access to capable and innovative businesses that can provide the supplies, services, equipment, and solutions necessary to support direct patient care and advance the IHS mission: �To raise the physical, mental, social and spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level.� ? Join us September 28-29, 2026, and show Albuquerque Area IHS what your business can do! ?? Important Notice This Industry Day is being conducted for informational, outreach, and market research purposes. This event is not a bidder�s conference, solicitation, Request for Proposal, Request for Quote, promise to contract, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. Participation in this event does not guarantee consideration for or award of any future procurement. The Government will not assume liability for costs incurred by any participant associated with attending the event or preparing, submitting, or presenting information, capability statements, presentations, or other materials. Costs incurred in response to this notice will not be considered allowable direct or indirect charges to the Government.
